newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down 2.60 pct at new 5-1/2 yr low.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down 2.60 pct at new 5-1/2 yr low.

text.p: Thai stocks took severe battering on Wednesday losing another 2.60 percent to close at its lowest level since October 1991.

Brokers said market jitters over a slowing economy, weak corporate earnings and bank loan quality forced the SET Index to finish 16.71 points lower at 626.57. The SET 50 fell 1.39 points, or 2.94 percent, to close at 45.96 on moderate 3.74 billion baht turnover.
Late afternoon buying by local mutual funds helped pare heavier losses which took the index down to an intra-day low of 618.66, brokers said.
"I heard local mutual funds bought blue chips such as Siam Cement and PTT," said a trader affiliated with Bangkok Bank.

Renewed concerns over bank loan quality hit finance and securities stocks as investors opted to sell ahead of compulsory disclosure of non-performing assets by the sectors from the end of the second quarter, traders said.
"I think investors are scared about the level of non-performing loans in the finance sector," said the trader.
The finance counter, which lost 3.93 percent, is saddled with deteriorating property and consumer hire purchase loans, analysts said.
They said finance firms continue facing high funding costs and dwindling broking revenues. Slow progress on their mergers eroded sentiment.
Economic concerns aggravated losses. Analysts forecast the economy would grow at its slowest pace in a decade low at about five percent in 1997 and corporate earnings would be weak.

Banks shed 2.94 percent, commerce 3.53 percent, and energy 2.53 percent. Slow business growth and industry liberalisation saw communications stocks fall 3.34 percent. Property, hit by a market glut, plunging asset values and liquidity problems fell 4.70 percent.
"Normally you need a catch, something to happen to stop a market like this from falling but I can't see it," said a foreign analyst.
Bangkok Bank shed eight baht to 164, TelecomAsia lost 2.25 to 35.50, and Siam Cement dropped 12 to 640. -- James Mclean (662) 652-0642
